Verified verbatim at src/components/AddBookModal.tsx:38-48; line 42 is `const base64 = (reader.result as string).split(',')[1];` and line 46 is `reader.readAsDataURL(file);`. A zero-byte PDF yields `'data:application/pdf;base64,'` and therefore `''`, not `undefined`; the `Promise<string>` contract at line 38 is not violated, and `summarizePdf('')` fails as an ordinary AI error rather than a type crash. CORRECTION TO THE MECHANISM: the discoverer blamed src/lib/storage/migrate.ts:125, but that line writes the SUMMARY's takeaway (`oneSentenceTakeaway: legacy.oneSentenceTakeaway ?? ''`), not the Book's. The actual violation is at src/lib/storage/migrate.ts:105-119, where `books.create({...})` sets `summaryId` (line 117) but OMITS `oneSentenceTakeaway` entirely — the field is not in the object literal at all. It compiles because the field is optional. So `book.oneSentenceTakeaway` is `undefined` for 100% of migrated legacy books, not just for the subset whose legacy takeaway was empty. Every legacy user therefore sees 'Not summarised yet' on every card in their library while opening any of those books shows the genuine takeaway in the orange panel — the two views contradict each other about every migrated book, deterministically. That is strictly stronger than the reported ''-valued case and matches this audit's already-established correction that the invariant is violated for real at migrate.ts:105-119. The type angle is legitimate and not a pattern-match: `oneSentenceTakeaway?` being optional while `summaryId?` is independently optional is exactly what lets migrate.ts construct the impossible state and compile. Severity stays `medium` — a durable, deterministic, user-visible inconsistency, but cosmetic in consequence (no crash, no data loss).
verifications.reachability: Deterministic on the legacy-migration path, which every pre-IndexedDB user hits exactly once. `migrateLegacyData` (src/lib/storage/migrate.ts:80) runs when `booksum_library_*` keys exist and the `booksum.migratedAt` marker is unset (lines 81-84); every book it creates gets `summaryId` but no `oneSentenceTakeaway`. verifications.verifierNote: Pattern present, but the stated failure scenario is factually wrong and the assertion holds at runtime — amending medium -> low. Verified verbatim at src/components/ProfileView.tsx:113-117: `const reader = new FileReader(); reader.onload = async (e) => { try { const content = e.target?.result as string;`, with `reader.readAsText(file)` at line 142. The typing analysis is correct as far as it goes — `ProgressEvent.target` is `EventTarget | null` and `FileReader.result` is `string | ArrayBuffer | null`, so the honest type is `string | ArrayBuffer | null | undefined` and `as string` collapses four possibilities into one. THE FAILURE SCENARIO DOES NOT HOLD: the finding says 'on an aborted or failed read `result` is null', but `FileReader` fires `load` only on successful termination — a failed read fires `error` and an abort fires `abort`, and neither routes to `reader.onload`. Inside this handler `e.target` is always the FileReader and `result` is always the `readAsText` string. So `JSON.parse(null)` is never actually invoked here. (I did confirm the mechanic in isolation under node — `JSON.parse(null)` coerces to `'null'` and returns `null`, which would make line 119's `data.books` throw — but that path is unreachable from `onload`.) The assertion is therefore runtime-correct, which the spec's verification criterion 2 says is a lower-severity outcome: 'A perfect match with the cast still loses (could've been a real type), but lower-severity.' The genuinely damaging cast in this handler is the NEXT line — `const data = JSON.parse(content) as LibraryExport;` at ProfileView.tsx:117, which is already filed and confirmed at `high` as F051. Standalone, line 116 is a lie with no victim, so `low` is the honest calibration. The fix is still worth the two lines because it removes the lie and, when combined with the F051 guard, produces a truthful error message instead of the generic 'Could not read that backup file.'
verifications.reachability: The assertion never misfires on a reachable path. Profile -> Data Management -> Import Data (ProfileView.tsx:327-333) -> `handleImport` (line 109) -> `reader.readAsText(file)` (line 142); `onload` runs only on success, where `result` is a string. Read failures and aborts bypass this handler entirely — and note there is no `reader.onerror` handler at all here, so a failed read currently produces silence rather than a wrong value.
verifications.blastRadius: One `onload` handler in one component. `content` feeds exactly one expression, `JSON.parse(content)` at line 117. No test file exists for ProfileView (src/components/ contains zero *.test.tsx).
